catch_records.source_excerpt: The Pacific Queen returned this morning with 149 Yellowfin Tuna and 61 Skipjacks for their 2 day trip with 24 anglers.

The Sea Watch on their 3/4 day local trip finished up with 42 Yellowfin Tuna, and 40 Skipjack! A 20lb flyline setup with a #4 hook or a small metal jig has been very effective for these fish! The Sea Watch is a definite run for both Tuesday and Wednesdays trips. Come on down for some fun fall fishing!

The San Diego on their full day reported in with 72 Yellowfin Tuna, and 123 Skipjack. Passports are Not currently required for this trip. Recommended setups for the San Diego has been a 20lb-25lb setup along with a 30lb-40lb setup for anchovies and sardines. Small jigs have been seeing decent response for the anglers looking to throw artificials.

southern_california.text: The marine pattern is improving through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 3-14 kt; morning is favored on 6 of 7 days. Combined seas range 3.0-6.0 ft with 6-16 sec periods. Best current windows: 11-08 AM, 11-09 AM, 11-06 AM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: There were a few anglers who went up the coast and caught some sea bass and rock fish. There have been some halibut caught near Davenport and Scott's Creek. The blue fin are still being caught near Monterey and now in front of Santa Cruz. There were bluefin caught around 36'44/122'13 and 36'40/122'15. There have been some bluefin caught as close as 10 miles from Santa Cruz. The wind was a little up and down today. The swell is a little bigger.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast October 22, 2026 Bluefin Tuna Give North Coast Anglers a Reason for Optimism Bluefin tuna are making a late-season appearance off the North Coast. Jake Mitchell of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing and fellow anglers from Shelter Cove have landed bluefin weighing 30 to 60 pounds, with most of the action occurring 10 to 30 miles offshore. Photo courtesy of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing. After hearing reports of bluefin tuna being caught out of Fort Bragg, Jake Mitchell of Sea Hawk Sport Fishing and a few other boats from Shelter Cove decided it was worth taking a look. Last Thursday, as they headed southwest from the Cove, they came across a couple of schools of bluefin. “We were lucky to get one fish that day,” said Mitchell. “Since then, there have been 11 more bluefin landed, with Monday being the most productive day.” The fleet grew by Wednesday, but the fishing had slowed. “I don’t think there’s a big concentration of fish out there, but that could change,” Mitchell said. “Most of the fish have been caught between 10 and 30 miles offshore. They haven’t been huge, but most are running between 30 and 60 pounds. Trolling Madmacs and spreader bars has worked for us.” Conditions

field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: We had amazing Lingcod fishing this morning on the Tacklebuster and the Surfrider. Both vessels had over 30+ Lingcod for each boat. That is a whole bunch of the "toothy critters". The rockfish were also biting with really good scores on them as well. We have one more day of good ocean weather tomorrow and then the ocean seems to be blowing up again the start of next week. It looks like lots of swell hitting the area next week and beyond for the beginning of November. Keep in touch with our office for weather changes or trips scheduled.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
